Question1:
1. Menu-Based Operation
Write a Java program where the following variables are already given:
int choice = 3;
int a = 20;
int b = 5;

Use a do-while loop and switch-case to perform the operation based on choice.
- 1 â†’ Addition
- 2 â†’ Subtraction
- 3 â†’ Multiplication
- 4 â†’ Division
- 5 â†’ Exit
- Use break after executing each case.
- The loop should continue until choice becomes 5.
Expected Output:
Multiplication = 100

Code:
package dailyAssignment;

public class Program_MenuBasedOperation {

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		// TODO Auto-generated method stub
		int choice = 3;
		int a = 20;
		int b = 5;
		do {
			
		switch(choice)
		{
		case 1: 
		  int sum=a+b;
		System.out.println("Addition = "+sum);break;
		case 2:
			int sub=a-b;
			System.out.println("Subtration = "+sub);break;
		case 3:
			int mul=a*b;
			System.out.println("Multiplication = "+mul);break;
		case 4: 
			int div=a/b;
			System.out.println("Division = "+div);break;
		case 5: System.out.println("Exit");
		
		}

		
		choice++;
		break;
		}while(choice<=5);
	}

}

Output:

Multiplication = 100



Question2:
2. Skip Even Numbers
Write a Java program to print numbers from 1 to 20 using a do-while loop.
Requirements:
- Use continue to skip all even numbers.
- Print only odd numbers.
- Use break to stop the loop when the number becomes greater than 15.
Expected Output:
1
3
5
7
9
11
13
15

Code:
package dailyAssignment;

public class Program_DowhileLoop {

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		// TODO Auto-generated method stub
		int num=0;
		do {
			num++;
			if(num%2==0)
				 continue;
			System.out.println(num+" ");
			if(num==15)
 				break;
		}while(num<=20);
		
		System.out.println();

	}

}

Output:
1 
3 
5 
7 
9 
11 
13 
15
